2. Sahani Bibi, the predecessors of the petitioners as the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title to 44½ decimals of land of the northern portion of C.S. Plot no. 114 under Khatian No. 124 of Mouza Brahmancharan stating, inter alia, that C.S. Plot No. 112 measuring .53 acre and C.S Plot No. 114 measuring .89 acre of Mouza Brahmancharan were owned by Sk. Mainuddin, who orally sold the same to Chand Bepari at a consideration of Tk. 75/-; Chand Bepari died leaving two sons and 5 daughters; these heirs of Chand Bepari instituted Title Suit No. 167 of 1916 against their co-sharers, Sultan Hossain and others for partition of joint properties, including the aforesaid two plots, in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka; this partition suit was decreed on contest and plaintiffs of that suit got saham which included the aforesaid two Plot Nos. 112 and 114 and the plaintiffs of that suit took possession through Court; by amicable partition Saburunnessa and Jahura Bibi got those two plots in their Saham and sold those two Plots with some other lands to Kari Samiruddin Ahmed by registered sale deed dated 10.04.22 and Kari Samiruddin took possession of his purchased land; Kari Samiruddin. by a registered deed dated 30.05.29 gifted half of the aforesaid Plots to Munshi Md. Nawab Ali who, in his turn, transferred the same to Sarma Sundari Guha by registered sale deed dated 05.01.30; by amicable partition amongst the co-shares, Sarma Sundari Guha got the northern portion of the Plot Nos. 112 and 114 and subsequently sold the same to Rdmjan Ali by registered deed of sale dated 08.12.38; Ramjan Ali died leaving wife Faizun Nessa Bibi, 5 sons Abbas Ali, Ahmed Ali, Ansar, Abdur Razzak and Md. Giasuddin and two daughters, Amena Khatun and Sahera Khatun; 34 acre of Plot No. 114 was recorded in the name of Faizunnessa in the State Acquisition Khatian as Plot No. 473 and .37 acre of Plot No. 114 was recorded in the name of Shamsuddin Mia (who purchased from Asahuddin Mia purchaser from heir of Md. Nowab Ali Mia) and the remaining 18 decimals of the said Plot was recorded in the name of Province of East Pakistan in the khan Khatian No. 1; all the heirs of said Ramjan Ali transferred 31½ decimals of land to Sahani Bibi. predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and 13 decimal of land to Md. Son Mia from Plot No. 114 by two separate sale deeds dated 16.02.65 and the purchasers were given possession in their respective land; Md. Sona Mia subsequently. transferred his 13 decimals of land to Sahani Bibi by registered sale deed dated 12.11.66 and put her in possession of the same Sahani Bibi. predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners, thus acquired total 441/2, decimals of land in the northern portion of C.S. Plot No. 114 and got her name mutated in the' S.A Khatian in place or Faizunnessa (wile of Ramjan Ali) and others in respect of 34 decimals and mutation of 10½ decimals was done through Court by a proceeding under section I 43A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act; Sahani Bibi paid rent in respect of the said land upto 1983; Sabani Bibi has been in possession all along cultivating land through laborers and growing cauli flowers and paddy etc. therein and R.S. record was prepared in her name; defendants claimed title to the suit land as grand children of Sk. Moinuddin (defendant of Title Suit No. 167 of 1916) and got the R.S. record changed in their names; such action having clouded the title of the plaintiff (Sabani Bibi) she was constrained to institute the suit. 

 8. As regards next submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioners that the Courts below illegally have not relied upon documents filed by the plaintiff which are subsequent to the decree of the same may be ancient antiquity but no presumption is attached to them being private documents and the plaintiff as well could not prove the same inasmuch the basic document was found to be interpolated in respect of Plot No. 124 making the same to be Plot No. 114 by over writing inasmuch as Ext. 6 shows that Sarma Sundari Guha transferred 44½ decimals of land from plot No. 114 whereas the schedule of Ext 5 showed she purchased only .2 decimals of Plot No. 114 and as such could not transfer 44½ to Remjan Ali and his heirs could not transfer .3½ and  13 decimals of land to Sahana Bibi and Sona Miah by Exts. 7 and 8 respectively inasmuch as Ext. 13, the rent receipt in favour of Ramjan Ali, the predecessor of plaintiff had not been proved by producing counter foils or adducing evidence through witnesses to prove the same as required in accordance with law and as such the plaintiff could not fall back upon the same as a basic documents of title of the suit land. Ext. 5 the document of transfer in favour of Sarma Sundari Guha by Munshi Nawab Ali (which is interpolated as to the C.S Plot No. 114 in place of C.S Plot No. 124 ) show only 02 acres of land out of the suit plot was transferred and as such she was not competent to transfer 44½ decimals of land to Ramjan Ali, who could only transfer .02 decimals by Exts. 7 and 8 to the plaintiff and Sona Mia.
